zormim.title: Zormim Hayarkon
body: Rebranding and social experience concept for Yarkon Park. "Zormim Layarkon" is a conceptual rebranding project for Yarkon Park, centered around the idea of the park as a restorative environment within the urban landscape of Tel Aviv. The project explores how design and digital interaction can encourage people to reconnect with nature, community, and slower experiences within the city.

The project combines branding, UX/UI design, and environmental thinking through a social mobile app designed specifically for the visitors of the park, and the people who live nearby. The app acts as a community-driven platform where users can create and join activities taking place throughout the park, from birdwatching sessions and meditation gatherings to sports meetups and creative workshops. Existing businesses and attractions within the park can also promote events and offer special benefits for app users.

The visual identity is inspired by the hidden ecosystem of the Yarkon and the animals that inhabit it, many of which visitors are not aware of. Illustrated animals appear throughout the branding system, app experience, and environmental signage, helping visitors feel more connected to the park's natural environment.

As part of the project, I also designed a branded picnic kit available for rent throughout the park, including blankets, cups, hats, and additional accessories intended to encourage longer, more social stays outdoors. Designated "Chill Points" were placed around quieter areas of the park, allowing users to activate guided meditations and calming experiences directly through the app.
The project was created as part of the course Design Language: Place at Shenkar College under the instruction of Efrat Nir.

cloud-nine.title: Cloud Nine
body: Cloud Nine is a fictional vitamin company designed for young adults who are navigating life on their own for the first time. Often struggling with unhealthy eating habits and a lack of structured routines, these individuals are in need of a personalized health approach. Through a simple process, customers send in their blood tests, and medical professionals recommend specific vitamins tailored to their needs.

Along with the vitamins, customers receive detailed instructions on when, how, and with what to take them. The product packaging features cute cloud creatures that represent the benefits of each vitamin, accompanied by small stickers with fun facts about each nutrient, making it both informative and engaging. This concept was created as part of a packaging course with our instructor, Sari Gabbai.

exponential.title: Exponential
body: Branding and interactive exhibition concept for Expo Tel Aviv's 100-year celebration of the Flying Camel Fair. "Exponential" is a conceptual technology pavilion created for Expo Tel Aviv's centennial celebration, inspired by the idea of exponential technological growth over the past 100 years. The project explores the dramatic evolution of technology by comparing the digital world of today to the early innovations presented during the original Flying Camel exhibitions.

The logotype was designed using a classical serif typeface that gradually transforms into its own pixelated version, symbolizing the accelerating transformation of technology over time. The Flying Camel symbol was redesigned in the same visual language, becoming a generative, distorted digital form.

Final visuals and motion-based typographic compositions were created using TouchDesigner, allowing the project's aesthetic to emerge through generative processes that directly support the concept itself. As part of the exhibition experience, visitors could interact with the pavilion's animated logo through body tracking technology (MediaPipe), using finger movement to control the logo's color spectrum in real time.
Created as part of the Multi-Platform Design course at Shenkar College, instructed by Nadav Barkan.
